content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To pronounce german words, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Study the unique sound of the German "W" (10 minutes)
Step 2. Research the uvular "R" pronunciation (1 hour)
Step 3. Identify the difference between "S" and "Z" sounds (15 minutes)
Step 4. Practice vocalizing the word "Eichhörnchen" (5 minutes)
Step 5. Record yourself saying long compound nouns (10 minutes)
Step 6. Learn the "CH" sound as in "Ich" (20 minutes)
Step 7. Learn the "CH" sound as in "Bach" (20 minutes)
Step 8. Review the pronunciation of the letter "V" (5 minutes)
Step 9. Memorize the vowel sounds for "A", "E", "I", "O", and "U" (2 hours)
Step 10. Practice the "F" sound for words starting with "V" (15 minutes)
Step 11. Study the German alphabet phonetics (3 hours)
Step 12. Listen to a German pronunciation podcast (45 minutes)
Step 13. Practice the "EU" and "ÄU" diphthongs (30 minutes)
Step 14. Practice the "V" sound in the word "Wasser" (2 minutes)
Step 15. Master the glottal stop between words (1 hour)
Step 16. Practice the "SCH" consonant cluster (10 minutes)
Step 17. Practice the long and short vowel distinctions (1 hour)
Step 18. Recite a list of common German verbs (20 minutes)
Step 19. Learn the "EI" and "IE" vowel combinations (40 minutes)
Step 20. Read a short German paragraph aloud (15 minutes)
Step 21. Study the "ST" and "SP" sounds at the start of words (25 minutes)
Step 22. Practice the "TS" sound for the letter "Z" (30 minutes)
Step 23. Practice the "PF" consonant combination (15 minutes)
Step 24. Look up the IPA symbols for German (1 hour)
Step 25. Learn the three German Umlauts: Ä, Ö, Ü (2 hours)
Step 26. Download a German language learning app (5 minutes)
Step 27. Study the "J" sound which is like English "Y" (10 minutes)
Step 28. Practice the "QU" sound (5 minutes)
Step 29. Practice words ending in "-ig" (15 minutes)
Step 30. Listen to German opera to hear clear diction (3 hours)
Step 31. Study the "TH" sound which is just a "T" (10 minutes)
Step 32. Watch a YouTube tutorial on German lip shapes (20 minutes)
Step 33. Practice the "AU" diphthong (15 minutes)
Step 34. Practice the trilled "R" versus the vocalic "R" (45 minutes)
Step 35. Learn the pronunciation of "-en" endings (15 minutes)
Step 36. Learn the pronunciation of the "B" at the end of words (10 minutes)
Step 37. Practice the "KN" sound where the "K" is not silent (20 minutes)
Step 38. Study word stress and syllable emphasis (1 hour)
Step 39. Mimic a native speaker's intonation (2 hours)
Step 40. Learn the "G" sound at the end of words (15 minutes)
Step 41. Practice the "D" sound at the end of words (10 minutes)
Step 42. Recite a German tongue twister (30 minutes)
Step 43. Practice the "NG" sound (10 minutes)
Step 44. Review the "H" sound when it is silent (10 minutes)
Step 45. Practice the "O" and "U" umlaut contrast (20 minutes)
Step 46. Learn the "PH" sound (5 minutes)
Step 47. Study the "Y" sound in German words (15 minutes)
Step 48. Buy a German-English dictionary with phonetic guides (30 minutes)
Step 49. Review the "C" sound in foreign loanwords (10 minutes)
Step 50. Listen to a German news broadcast (30 minutes)
Step 51. Practice sentence-level rhythm (45 minutes)
Step 52. Record a video of your mouth movements (15 minutes)
Step 53. Practice the "Ä" sound (10 minutes)
Step 54. Practice the "S" sound at the beginning of words (15 minutes)
Step 55. Study the "ẞ" (Eszett) character (20 minutes)
Step 56. Practice the "AI" and "AY" sounds (10 minutes)
Step 57. Practice the "Ö" sound (15 minutes)
Step 58. Find a list of German minimal pairs (20 minutes)
Step 59. Take a short quiz on German sounds (15 minutes)
Step 60. Practice the "X" sound (5 minutes)
